subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 31-year-old man is evaluated for episodic palpitations, tremor, and diaphoresis with a blood pressure of 190/105 mm Hg. Biochemical testing shows markedly increased plasma free metanephrines, and imaging confirms a right adrenal mass. Before surgery, the clinicians review the pathways that inactivate catecholamines so that they can interpret his urinary studies correctly.
question: Which of the following is the major urinary end product of norepinephrine and epinephrine catabolism?
explanation_correct: Norepinephrine and epinephrine are inactivated by catechol-O-methyltransferase, which forms normetanephrine and metanephrine, and by monoamine oxidase, and their final common urinary end product is vanillylmandelic acid. Dopamine is metabolized predominantly to homovanillic acid, whereas serotonin is degraded to 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid.

explanation_incorrect.A: Homogentisic acid accumulates in alkaptonuria because homogentisate oxidase is deficient; it is a tyrosine degradation intermediate, not a catecholamine metabolite.
explanation_incorrect.B: Homovanillic acid is the major metabolite of dopamine, not of norepinephrine and epinephrine.
explanation_incorrect.C: 5-Hydroxyindoleacetic acid is the degradation product of serotonin and is measured in carcinoid syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.E: 3-Hydroxybutyrate is a ketone body produced by hepatic fatty acid oxidation and is not a catecholamine metabolite.

educationalObjective: Vanillylmandelic acid is the major urinary end product of norepinephrine and epinephrine degradation by catechol-O-methyltransferase and monoamine oxidase.
